## METHOD

All probes ran against the pinned tree. Scratch output stayed under the session scratchpad; no repository file was created or modified except this report on its own branch.

**Source baselines (three independent extractions of the vendored PDF, plus renders).** (a) poppler `pdftotext` raw and `-layout`, split per page; (b) the importer's own `extractPdfText` (`extract.ts`, column-aware) dumped per page; (c) `pdfminer` per page, which maps the PDF's embedded Japanese CID font (`XQNONC+HiraKakuPro-W3`, Adobe-Japan1) that poppler and the bundle's pdfjs items drop; (d) `pdftoppm` renders at 70–400 dpi; (e) pdf.js 5 in headless Chromium with the Adobe-Japan1 CMaps loaded, as a second renderer. Decompressed page content streams were read directly (pypdf) where extraction disagreed with rendering.

**Source fidelity and provenance (bar conditions 1, 2, 7).**
- Every leaf declared `source-prose` by `field-provenance.json` (68 unscoped and 14 record-scoped declarations, classification re-implemented from `fieldProvenance.ts` precedence) was resolved across all 1,799 records: 10,768 leaves, 10,448 strings; 2,576 strings shorter than four characters were skipped as non-discriminating. Each remaining string (7,872) was required to be a whitespace-normalised, hyphen-cluster-normalised contiguous span of the pages its record locator (plus any matching `fieldLocators` entry) cites, in at least one of baselines (a)–(c). Result: 7,804 on the cited page(s); 11 only on an adjacent page (continuations whose owning text wraps; all verified as the same passage); 4 only under quote/dash folding; 8 found on another page (identical text printed elsewhere, e.g. the dragons' shared Frightful Presence, Travel Pace wrapped cells); 45 not found. The 45 were inspected one by one: 10 are interior table splices (finding A3-F2), 14 are bullet-glyph joins (A3-F2 sibling), 14 are Iron Flask d100 cells (A3-F1), 4 are Travel Pace wrapped cells and one split header (not defects, confirmed by render), 2 are Apparatus of the Crab lever cells printed in a two-column cell layout (confirmed by render), 1 is Rope of Climbing (`1-foot` hyphenated at a line end, not a defect).
- Every `source-prose` table cell (1,972 cells across 109 tables) was additionally checked against all three extractions of its cited pages: the only cells absent from every extraction are the 14 Iron Flask d100 cells, 94 class-table `—` cells whose pages carry no other em dash (see observations), 3 Apparatus cells and 1 Short-Term Madness cell (both confirmed against the render).
- Locators: the `source` label equals `SRD 5.1 <locator>` for all 1,799 records; the licence block equals the manifest's for all 1,799; `sourceRef` equals the manifest's `sourceUrl` for all; 344 records carry `fieldLocators` (`spell /classes` 319, `equipment /capacity` 13, `class /primaryAbilities` 12). The copied Champion Additional Fighting Style options cite p. 24 per option (`options[].source`) while the record cites p. 25, so the L1-F1 class does not recur there.
- `source-region-ledger.json`: 2,787 entries, `unrepresented` 0, `unemitted` 0, `unaccountedPages` []; entries for the suspect tables (Bard, Sorcerer, Wizard, Travel Pace, Iron Flask) were read.

**Typed projections vs prose (sampled across every record kind and the full page range).**
- Creatures: all 514 attack objects (actions, reactions, legendary actions, traits of 317 creatures and 2 stat blocks) were parsed from their verbatim lead-in text and compared on attack type, bonus, reach/range, target and every hit-damage component; 512 parsed, 2 (Druid, Dryad shillelagh forms) reviewed by hand. All 272 entries carrying a `DC N <Ability> saving throw` were compared with `mechanics.saves`. Result: two disagreements (A3-F3); six traits with formula DCs carry the ability without a DC (not a disagreement).
- Spells: all 319 spell headers were located in the importer extraction and compared on level, school, ritual flag, casting time, range, components letters and duration; concentration flag vs duration; damage dice in prose vs `mechanics.damage`; typed `upcast` dice-per-slot operations and `scaling.perSlot` vs `higherLevels`. No disagreement (12 spells with a `perSlot` scaling of "one additional target" carry no `increase` field, Fire Shield and Spirit Guardians carry `typeOptions`, Wish's stress damage is unprojected prose).
- Magic items: 239 of 240 header lines located (Amulet of Proof Against Detection wraps); `itemType`, `rarity` (verbatim multi-rarity strings), `requiresAttunement`, `attunementRequirement` agree.
- Equipment: rows rebuilt from pdfjs item coordinates for pp. 62–74; 208 of 219 records located by name; cost, weight, damage die and type, AC, Strength requirement, stealth disadvantage, speed, carrying capacity and properties agree (11 unlocated are qualified names or footnote rows already matched on cost; `capacity` is cited to the Container Capacity table by field locator).
- Class tables: `table:the-bard` and `table:the-monk` compared cell by cell with the renders of pp. 11 and 26 (levels, bonus, features, known/slots/ki/martial-arts columns agree); 484 unavailable cells are discussed under observations.
- Ancestries (13): size, speed, ability-score increases and languages read against the SRD; all agree. Conditions (15): `mechanics.effects` read against the bullet lists; all agree. Hazards (25): every printed DC appears in mechanics or is a disclosed unprojected clause; dice agree. Feature resources (12 sampled, including the registry-repaired Indomitable, Arcane Recovery, Divine Sense): agree.

**Provenance classes and composition.** Declarations were read in full (238), including the 14 record-scoped `source-derived` declarations introduced by the L1-F2 repair; the splice producers (`stripEmbeddedTableProse.ts` vs `parseRules`/`parseGamemasteringRules`/`parseConditions`/`parseEquipmentGuidance`) were traced to explain the residual.

**Discovery.** `record-relationships.json` (29 declarations) was resolved with the repository's own `resolveRecordRelationships` over the bundled pack: 854 declared occurrences, 852 `resolved`, 2 `excluded`, 0 `unresolved-target`, 0 `indeterminate`. A census of undeclared leaves whose value equals an existing record key found 51 (kind, pointer) shapes (largest: `class/progression/*/advancement/*/ref` 202, `magic-item/mechanics/effects/*/spellRef` 142, `class/features/*` 123), and of undeclared condition-name leaves 12 shapes (creature actions 218, traits 110, legendary 30, conditionImmunities 35, magic-item 27, ancestry 5, equipment 2, reaction 1), confirming the candidate record's disclosed limits are accurate and still limits. `ruleAwareness` was exercised for seven keys. Real context packets were rendered through `runDiscoveryStages` + `renderContextPacketMessage` for diagnostic probes P1, P2, P3, P5, P7 and P8 and their provenance headings, projection-limit notes, capability sections and known-limit sections read.

**Readiness.** All 1,369 `executionReadiness` clauses of the 240 magic items were tabulated (green 241, engine-pending 769, adjudicated-by-design 358, design-blocked 1, none transitional/red). Green clauses were cross-tabulated by representation block and hooks (structuredField 94, operations with F5 recharge 51, hook-free economies 26, F5 per-period 20, …); `LANDED_MAGIC_ITEM_ENGINE_HOOKS` (10 hook keys) and `MAGIC_ITEM_PASSIVE_EFFECT_RUNTIME_CONSUMERS` (empty, L3-F1) were read against `validateMagicItemClausesAndClassify`, `assertMagicItemOperationReady` and the runtime owners named for each landed hook (`itemResetExecutor.ts`, `itemState.ts`, `activeEffects.ts`, `rest.ts` all present). The 26 hook-free green economies are single-use, dose and at-will economies that `useItem` spends without a recharge responsibility.

**Adjudication support.** All 77 registered tools were dumped with description and input schema; 23 mutation/resolution tool descriptions were read against the SRD rules they cite (ties, resistance order, death saves, instant death, suffocation, bonus-action spells, attunement limits, prepared-spell counts, ammunition recovery) and against the ledger contracts and `RULE_KNOWN_LIMITS` statements (all 17 statements name registered participants; the `rule:hiding` tie claim and `rule:weapon-properties` recovery claim match the tool descriptions and `toolRecoverAmmunition.ts`).

## FINDINGS

### A3-F1 | NON-BLOCKER | Iron Flask d100 column carries an invented leading zero and a normalised dash in cells declared verbatim source prose

- **Invariant and authority.** `source-prose` is "literal text reproduced from the source. The only class a consumer may present as verbatim source authority" (`packages/core/src/rules/fieldProvenance.ts`); the unscoped declaration `(table, /rows)` reads "the table's raw cells, reproduced verbatim from the source table". Bar #2 (truthful provenance) and #7 (no compiler-authored content carries source provenance or the licence block); ADR 0007 §2–§4 and ADR 0020 §1 ("a discovery system whose retrieved passages are not faithful to the source … launders invented rules through an authoritative channel").
- **Evidence.** `records.json` `table:iron-flask` rows[0] is `["01–50","Empty"]`, rows[1] `["51–54", …]` (U+2013). The curated spec at `packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseDocumentTables.ts:961-1000` is a `reviewed-reconstruction` whose `sourceLines` are the extracted `'1 50'`, `'51 54'`, … and whose `rows` hand-write `'01–50'`, `'51–54'`. The source (SRD p. 228): the page content stream shows the glyph "1" in the text font, then CID 114 of the embedded Japanese CID font `C0_0`, then "50"; pdfminer decodes the row as `1‒50` (U+2012); pdf.js with CMaps renders `1–50`; poppler renders `1 50`. No "0" glyph precedes the "1" in the stream. The ledger entry `p228-l52-table-rows` records the source as "Empty 1 50 Demon (type 1) 51 54 …". The remaining 13 range cells differ from the source only by the dash code point (U+2012 printed, U+2013 emitted).
- **Reachability.** Live: `lookup_rules` returns the record and the context packet renders `/data/rows/0/0: 01–50` under "Source prose (verbatim; authoritative)" (classification verified through `classifyFieldPointer`).
- **Consequence.** A one-character compiler invention ("0") and a code-point normalisation are presented to the DM model as verbatim source text with the SRD licence block. Ruling impact is nil (the range is the same); the defect is provenance truthfulness.
- **Siblings.** Query: every `source-prose` table cell (1,972) against the three extractions of its cited pages. Only the Iron Flask column fails for this reason; every other d100 table (Teleport p. 186, Wand of Wonder, Efreeti Bottle, Bag of Beans, Deck of Illusions) prints `01–…` with U+2013 in the text layer and matches. The other `reviewed-reconstruction` specs (8) reproduce their source lines. Same class as o9bd.16 L1-F2 and registry `source-authority-fable-f5` (synthesised table text distinguished from source text).
- **Closure.** Either emit the printed cell (`1–50`, dash transcribed the same way the class-table dashes are) or scope `(table, /rows)` for `table:iron-flask` as `source-derived` with the reason, and regenerate. Evidence: a generalised invariant in the importer tests that every `source-prose` table cell occurs in a CMap-complete extraction of its cited pages (pdfminer-style decoding of the Japanese CID font) unless a scoped declaration covers it; the Iron Flask cells are the exact reproducer to pin.
- **Recurrence alias.** o9bd.16 L1-F2; registry `source-authority-fable-f5`.

### A3-F2 | NON-BLOCKER (recurrence of the o9bd.16 L1-F2 interior-splice class repaired in `.16.7.5`) | Ten records with a table spliced out of the interior of a `source-prose` field keep the verbatim class; bullet-list joins are a lower-consequence sibling

- **Invariant and authority.** Same as A3-F1 (`fieldProvenance.ts` class definition, bar #2/#7). The project's own disposition in o9bd.16 L1-F2 (`.16.7.5`): "Descriptions with a printed table spliced out of their interior also kept the verbatim class … the compiler derives scoped source-derived declarations from that report; nothing is hand-listed. A trailing or leading trim that leaves a contiguous quotation stays source-prose." Design §7.2 requires in-band disclosure of what a projection omits; the packet heading "Source prose (verbatim; authoritative)" is the model-facing claim.
- **Evidence.** The contiguity check (every `source-prose` string must be a contiguous span of its cited pages in at least one extraction) leaves these ten as the only non-trivial residual: `rule:ability-checks` (Typical Difficulty Classes table removed between "…shows the most common DCs." and "To make an ability check…", p. 77), `rule:ability-scores-and-modifiers` (p. 76), `rule:expenses-lifestyle-expenses` (pp. 72–73), `rule:half-dragon-template` (pp. 320–321), `rule:hit-points` (Hit Dice by Size, pp. 255–256), `rule:objects` (two tables, p. 203), `rule:services` (p. 74), `rule:skills` (the per-ability skill list, pp. 77–78; carried as `skillsByAbility`), `rule:speed` (Travel Pace, p. 84), and `condition:exhaustion` `/description` (the six-level table removed between "…as specified in the effect's description." and "If an already exhausted creature…", p. 358; carried as `/levels`). `field-provenance.json` has record-scoped `source-derived` declarations only for the `stripEmbeddedTableProse.ts` producer (6 spells, 4 features, 9 magic items) and two folded-row tables; none for `rule /text` or `condition /description`. The spliced tables are linked by `tableRefs` on the nine rules, so content is not lost.
  Sibling (lower consequence): 11 condition descriptions (`blinded`, `charmed`, `frightened`, `grappled`, `invisible`, `paralyzed`, `petrified`, `prone`, `restrained`, `stunned`, `unconscious`) equal the printed bullet items joined with spaces and the `•` glyphs removed, while the declaration reason says "the condition's intro line, quoted verbatim" (these conditions print no intro line); `feat:grappler` and `feature:monk:martial-arts` join bulleted lists the same way. Class `startingEquipment/text` keeps its bullets, so the treatment is producer-dependent.
- **Reachability.** Live: `lookup_rules` and the context packet (`rule:*`, `condition:*` candidates are must-consider material in P5 and the rule probes).
- **Consequence.** The DM model is told the spliced text is verbatim and contiguous; the omitted region is signposted only by the prose's own "the X table shows" and the `tableRefs`/`levels` links. No rule content is invented or lost. The prior round rated this class a BLOCKER before repair; acceptance should disposition the recurrence explicitly rather than inherit the closed status of `.16.7.5`.
- **Siblings.** Query: the contiguity check over all 7,872 checked `source-prose` strings (membership listed above; nothing else of this class survives). Rule records with `tableRefs` (32) whose table is appended at the end rather than removed from the interior remain contiguous and are not members.
- **Closure.** Route the rule/gamemastering/equipment-guidance and condition table strips through the same internal-splice report the L1-F2 repair built, so the compiler emits scoped `source-derived` declarations for these ten (or keep the pre-splice verbatim text and strip only at display). For the bullet joins, either keep the printed `•` markers or declare the composed `description` `source-derived` with the correct reason. Evidence: a generalised contiguity invariant (every `source-prose` leaf is a contiguous span of the importer extraction of a cited page, modulo whitespace and hyphen clusters) in the importer tests, with these records as the reproducer set.
- **Recurrence alias.** o9bd.16 L1-F2 (`.16.7.4`/`.16.7.5` sibling); registry `source-authority-opus-f19` class.

### A3-F3 | NON-BLOCKER | Two creature attack projections disagree with the printed stat block (Flying Snake drops a printed damage component; Jackal projects an attack with no damage because the printed minus is U+2013), without in-band disclosure

- **Invariant and authority.** Registry row `creature-statblock-mechanics` (alias `sol:CAP-004`, narrowed): "emitted creature attack/damage projections agree with the printed stat block"; row `unicode-minus-damage` (`opus:F-29`, accepted): "printed U+2212 in attack Hit-clause dice normalizes to ASCII"; design §7.2: a partial projection must disclose what it omits in band. Bar #1 (source fidelity) and #9 (explicit limits).
- **Evidence.** `creature:flying-snake` `actions[0]` text "Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1 piercing damage plus 7 (3d4) poison damage." (SRD p. 372, verified on the page); `mechanics.attacks[0].hitDamage` is `[{average 7, dice 3d4, type poison}]` and `mechanics.damage` the same: the printed 1 piercing damage is absent. `creature:jackal` `actions[0]` text "…Hit: 1 (1d4 – 1) piercing damage." (pp. 382–383; the importer extraction carries U+2013 at that position); `mechanics.attacks[0]` is `{attackType, attackBonus 1, reachFeet 5, target}` with no `hitDamage` and no `mechanics.damage`. Neither record carries any note; the packet's projection-limit notes cover only success branches, areas and readiness.
- **Reachability.** Model-facing only: `lookup_rules` and the packet's "Typed projection" partition. No runtime code consumes creature `hitDamage` (`grep hitDamage packages/core/src` matches only `kindSchemas.ts`).
- **Consequence.** A DM model that reads the typed projection as the attack's damage understates the Flying Snake's bite (poison only, no piercing) and sees a Jackal attack that appears to deal no damage; the verbatim text beside it is correct, so the error is recoverable but undisclosed.
- **Siblings.** Query 1: all 514 attack objects parsed from their lead-in text (512 parsed, 2 hand-checked): these are the only two disagreements. Query 2: all 19 Hit clauses with a flat (dice-less) component: 18 project `{amount: 1, type}` correctly; Flying Snake is the only "flat plus dice" form in the corpus. Query 3: dash characters inside creature entry dice expressions: U+2212 ×3 (normalised by the F-29 repair), U+2013 ×1 (Jackal), so the en-dash variant is the single uncovered sibling of `opus:F-29`.
- **Closure.** Extend the attack grammar to the "N type damage plus M (dice) type" form and to a U+2013 minus (or make the Jackal attack fail closed as a whole and disclose the unprojected Hit clause), regenerate, and pin both records in `creatureAttackLeadIns.ts`/`parseCreatures.test.ts`. Evidence: a generalised invariant that for every attack lead-in whose Hit clause parses, `hitDamage` lists every printed damage component (the corpus-wide parse used here reproduces it).
- **Recurrence alias.** registry `unicode-minus-damage` (`opus:F-29`) and `creature-statblock-mechanics` (`sol:CAP-004`).

## NO-REQUIREMENT OBSERVATIONS

- Class-table unavailable cells (484 `—` cells in the eight spellcaster/warlock tables): the source encodes each as CID 138 of the embedded Japanese CID font (Adobe-Japan1 → U+0336 via pdfminer; 74 runs on the Bard page content stream, matching the registry's count), which poppler neither extracts nor renders; pdf.js with CMaps renders a dash. The pack's `—` is a transcription consistent with the accepted registry row `table-empty-cells`. The importer README's "Blank vs. dash cells" paragraph still states the opposite (stale documentation; the README is not an in-band §5.1–§5.6 artifact).
- Bundle G-capabilities fails in this environment only because the Dolt-gated `checkpoint.doltRepo.test.ts` did not execute; the gate fails closed as designed and the lane prompt anticipated the skip.
- The bundle README names the undeclared condition-name leaves as "creature, ancestry and magic-item records"; the census also finds two `equipment/useProfile` leaves (`ball-bearings` `failureCondition: prone`, `net` `condition: restrained`). The candidate record's kind-agnostic wording covers them.
- Importer README staleness: deity Symbol cells are described as emitted without apostrophes, but the pack carries the reconstructed `Mare's head` etc. (verified against the page); counts "108 table records"/"314 rule records" vs 109/325 in the pack.
- Champion Additional Fighting Style options cite p. 24 per option while the record cites p. 25; the per-option `source` field is the mechanism the L1-F1 repair chose, so no requirement is violated.
- Travel Pace cells `400 feet`, `4 miles`, … are wrapped cells in print (render verified), not compositions; the composed column headers are already scoped `source-derived`.
- `rule:cover` carries no capability binding, known limit or relationship; the packet states "no capability was positively selected" with the ADR 0020 §3 disclaimer, which is the permitted empty statement.

## LIMITS

- No live play, no model calls, no Dolt; the discovery pipeline was exercised offline through the diagnostic fixtures (P1, P2, P3, P5, P7, P8) only.
- Verbatim checks are string-contiguity checks; they cannot detect a wrong owner whose text is identical elsewhere (8 such strings were accepted on that basis) or a correctly anchored span attached to the wrong record when the span is also printed on the cited page.
- Typed-projection checks were corpus-wide only for creature attacks, creature save DCs, spell headers/concentration/damage dice/upcast, magic-item headers and equipment table rows; magic-item `effects`, operations, economies, state machines and entity grants were not re-read against the source beyond the registry's own `magicItemEffectSourceAgreement` test (green in G-suite); class progression tables were checked by eye for Bard and Monk only; feature `mechanics` beyond resources, hazard projections beyond DC/dice parity, and `useProfile` clauses were spot-read, not enumerated.
- Readiness was judged from the classifier, the landed-hook registry and the presence of each named runtime owner; individual runtime paths behind the 10 landed hooks were not re-executed (L4/L5 territory).
- Tool descriptions were read for 23 of 77 tools; `run()` validation code was read only for `resolve_check`, `recover_ammunition` and `lookup_rules`.
- The beads database was unavailable, so bead notes (including the L1 lane's full LIMITS) were not read; the finding registry and the two audit documents were the only disposition inputs.
- Renders used poppler and pdf.js only; no Acrobat/pdfium comparison.

LANE RESULT: NO BLOCKER FOUND WITHIN STATED DENOMINATORS
